description: Labeled citations for ATT&CK output grounding benchmark. Each case has an answer fragment, retrieved context, and gold labels per technique ID.

label_schema.REAL_AND_PLAUSIBLE: Real technique and relevant to retrieved context (should NOT be treated as an error)
label_schema.REAL_BUT_IRRELEVANT: Real technique but not supported by retrieved context (should be flagged)
label_schema.FABRICATED: Technique ID does not exist in ATT&CK (should be flagged)
label_schema.REVOKED: Technique exists but is revoked/deprecated (should be flagged)

cases.answer: Ransomware often uses T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact to encrypt files and block recovery.
cases.retrieved_context: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability of system and network resources. They may encrypt data on a large scale to prevent recovery without a decryption key. This is Data Encrypted for Impact.

cases.answer: The malware performs process injection consistent with T1055.
cases.retrieved_context: Adversaries may inject code into processes in order to evade process-based defenses and potentially elevate privileges. Process injection is a method of executing arbitrary code in the address space of a separate live process.

cases.answer: Attackers dumped credentials from LSASS using T1003 OS Credential Dumping.
cases.retrieved_context: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material, normally in the form of a hash or clear text password, from the operating system and software. Credential dumping techniques include accessing LSASS memory.

cases.answer: Execution was performed via T1059.001 PowerShell.
cases.retrieved_context: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution. PowerShell is a powerful interactive command-line interface and scripting environment included in the Windows operating system.

cases.answer: Persistence was established with T1053.005 Scheduled Task.
cases.retrieved_context: Adversaries may abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code. Scheduled tasks can be used for persistence.

cases.answer: The activity is consistent with T1055 process injection.
cases.retrieved_context: Sequential port scanning was observed across multiple internal hosts. No process memory or injection activity was recorded. Network reconnaissance only.

cases.answer: This maps to T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact.
cases.retrieved_context: Spearphishing emails with malicious attachments were delivered to finance staff. The campaign focused on credential theft via fake login pages. No file encryption was observed.

cases.answer: The adversary used T1003 to access credentials.
cases.retrieved_context: Large volumes of data were transferred to an external IP over HTTPS. Exfiltration over web service channels was the primary observed behavior. No credential dumping tools were present.

cases.answer: Lateral movement used T1021.002 SMB/Windows Admin Shares.
cases.retrieved_context: Files on the desktop were encrypted with a custom algorithm and renamed with a ransom extension. Shadow copies were deleted. No SMB authentication or share enumeration was logged.

cases.answer: Data left the network via T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel.
cases.retrieved_context: Code was injected into explorer.exe to evade process-based defenses. The injection used process hollowing. No outbound C2 exfiltration was described in the evidence.

cases.answer: The novel stealth module maps to T9999 Super Stealth Encryption.
cases.retrieved_context: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability and demand ransom payment.

cases.answer: Behavior matches T1234.999 Custom Kernel Hook.
cases.retrieved_context: Process injection into running processes was detected on several endpoints.

cases.answer: This is associated with T0000 Baseline Bypass.
cases.retrieved_context: Credential dumping from memory was observed using a Mimikatz-like tool.

cases.answer: Operators relied on T8888 Ghost Protocol for C2.
cases.retrieved_context: Outbound traffic over HTTPS to a suspicious domain was used for command and control.

cases.answer: The loader uses T7777.001 Memory-Only Implant.
cases.retrieved_context: A fileless implant resided only in memory and executed via PowerShell.

cases.answer: Scripts were run with T1086 PowerShell.
cases.retrieved_context: PowerShell was used to download and execute a remote payload interactively.

cases.answer: Encryption used T1486; a secondary module claimed T9999 for evasion.
cases.retrieved_context: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability of resources and demand ransom. Data Encrypted for Impact prevents recovery without a key.

cases.answer: Primary impact was T1486; analysts also noted T1055 without evidence of injection.
cases.retrieved_context: Widespread file encryption occurred across user directories. Ransom notes demanded payment for decryption keys. No process injection telemetry was present.

cases.answer: Activity involved T1003 for credentials, unsupported T1048 for exfil claims, and invented T9999.
cases.retrieved_context: LSASS memory was accessed to recover passwords and hashes. OS Credential Dumping was confirmed by EDR. No exfiltration channel was documented in the retrieved evidence.

cases.answer: The binary used T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information.
cases.retrieved_context: Adversaries may attempt to make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, or otherwise obfuscating its contents on the system or in transit.
